verses.text: Here’s what the LORD told Jeremiah.
“Get up and go down to the potter’s house. That’s where I’ll tell you what I have to say.”
So I went down to the potter’s house. Sure enough, there he was making something on the wheel.
The clay pot got messed up while he was shaping it. So he worked the clay into another pot, whatever shape seemed right to him.
Then the LORD spoke to me.
“Family of Israel, can’t I do with you what this potter does?” says the LORD. “Look, you’re in my hands, Israel, like clay in the potter’s hands.
The moment I say I’ll pull up a nation or kingdom, tear it down, and destroy it,
if the nation I’m talking about drops its evil ways, I’ll change my mind about the disaster I planned for it.
The moment I say I’ll build up a nation or kingdom and plant it,
if they do evil right in front of me and refuse to listen, I’ll change my mind about the good I said I’d do for them.

“So now tell the people of Judah and Jerusalem, ‘The LORD says, “Look, I’m shaping a disaster and making plans against you. Every one of you needs to turn from the evil you’re doing right now and change how you live.”’
But they say, ‘Forget it. We’ll follow our own plans. Every one of us will do what our stubborn, evil heart wants.’”
So the LORD says, “Go ask around among the nations, ‘Who’s ever heard anything like this?’ Israel, the young woman, has done something awful.
Does the snow of Lebanon vanish from the rocky heights? Do those cold streams flowing down from far away dry up?
But my people have forgotten me. They burn incense to false gods. They’ve been tripped up on the old paths and sent wandering off along side roads, where nobody even laid a proper road.
They’ll leave their land a shock to everyone, a place people hiss at from then on. Anyone who passes by will stare and shake their head.
I’ll scatter them in front of the enemy like an east wind scattering dust. When disaster hits, they’ll see my back instead of my face.”

Then they said, “Come on, let’s make a plan against Jeremiah. Priests will still have the law, wise people will still have advice, and prophets will still have a word for us. Let’s go after him with our words and ignore everything he says.”
Pay attention to me, LORD. Listen to what the people opposing me are saying.
Is this how good gets paid back, with evil? They’ve dug a pit to take my life. Remember how I stood before you and spoke up for them to turn your anger away.
So hand their children over to famine and give them over to the sword. Let their wives lose their children and become widows. Let their men be killed and their young men fall to the sword in battle.
Let cries come from their homes when you bring a band of attackers on them without warning. They dug a pit to catch me and hid traps where I’d step.
LORD, you know every plan they’ve made to kill me. Don’t forgive their wrongdoing or wipe their sin out of your sight. Let them fall before you. Deal with them when your anger comes.
